# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

# gh-807: [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Review verdicts must form one reconciled, authoritative state per (PR, head): contradictory verdicts on the same head must be resolved before any arming/merge decision, and the sticky-approval rule must bind the ARming side, not only the rework side.

## Subject

Review-leg verdict posting + tick's arming queries. Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 05:47:30Z and 05:47:40Z — two review legs posted **APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES verdicts 97 seconds apart on the SAME head**; PR state ended contradictory (`pr_approved` + `agent:rework` both applied). Root causes: (a) verdicts are posted as ISSUE comments, so `headMovedSinceLastReview`-style matching can never associate them; (b) no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side ignores the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

## Capability surface

- Verdict persistence: review leg writes a machine-readable verdict record (head sha + verdict + thread census) — file on `factory-data` or a PR comment with a parseable marker, not a free-form issue comment.
- Reconciliation: tick reads the latest verdict per head; if two verdicts exist for one head, newest wins and a WARN is logged; REQUEST_CHANGES from the newest leg blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review.
- Arming-side sticky approval: `agent:rework` arming requires the effective verdict != APPROVE (or unresolved BLOCKING threads), same rule the rework-side uses.
- Clean rollback: reconciliation must not fight the human review state (ruleset approvals untouched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: two verdicts on one head ⇒ tick logs `⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins` and uses the newest.
2. AC2: after reconciliation, `pr_approved` and `agent:rework` cannot coexist on one head (tick removes the loser label with a comment citing both verdict sources).
3. AC3: arming-side check: APPROVE verdict ⇒ no rework arm even when non-blocking threads exist (suggestions do NOT trigger rework).
4. AC4: verdict record is machine-parseable (structured marker), so no head-matching by comment text.
5. AC5: unit tests for the reconciliation; live verification on the next fa GOAL PR with a genuine CHANGES_REQUESTED.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (newest-wins, label reconciliation, APPROVE-blocks-rework-arm).
- L2: replay the #1428 97s-pair against the reconciler.
- L3 (live): one review cycle with contradictory injected verdicts in a scratch PR.

## Non-goals

- Changing what reviewers write in human-readable comments.
- Blocking merges on suggestion-tier threads (only BLOCKING gates).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428, verdicts 05:47:30Z/05:47:40Z 2026-10-09, `pr_approved`+`agent:rework` coexistence.
- Related: #806 (arming latch).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instruction…

5. `js/smAgent.js` — check reconcile_verdicts & arm_rework placement in processRule; check `ticket.issueNumber` availability; check github_remove_label global; check that arm_rework's reworkArmGate is only invoked in the right place.

Potential issues to investigate:

a) In `postPRReviewComments.js`, `postVerdictRecord` uses the global `github_get_pr` directly rather than the scm abstraction. The repo says "SCM abstraction: use js/common/scm.js (via configLoader.createScm(config)) instead of calling github_* or ado_* globals directly." But postPRReviewComments.js is GitHub-specific (posting to GitHub PR), and it already uses `gh` helpers. Let me check if postPRReviewComments.js already uses github_* globals elsewhere. Let me grep.

b) In smProvider.verdictRecords — ioCacheGet with kind 'prVerdicts'. Need to check ioCacheGet signature: ioCacheGet(owner, repo, kind, key)? And whether other provider methods use the same pattern. Also, "if (memo) return memo;" — an empty array is truthy? `[]` is truthy in JS, so that's fine. But `null`/`undefined` from a failed... actually ioCachePut always called, so fine.

c) The `latestVerdictRecord(prNumber, headSha)` in smProvider calls `this.verdictRecords(prNumber)` — relies on `this` binding. But one concern: `latestVerdict` guard semantics — `if (q.latestVerdict && (!lvVerdict || q.latestVerdict.indexOf(lvVerdict) === -1)) return false;` — right.

e) The reconcile rule in sm_github.json queries `labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` — OR semantics? Need to verify github source labels query is OR. The test asserts OR semantics ("either contradictory carrier matches (OR semantics — the action decides)"). Let me check githubSource to see how labels filter works. The test in test_smGithubSource 'latestVerdict: the reconcile rule matches exactly...' uses labels: ['pr_approved', 'agent:rework'] with prs labeled 'pr_approved' and it matched (items pr-81, pr-82). g) The arm gate is added to the `arm_rework` localAction in smAgent.js — this gates ALL rules with localAction arm_rework, which is what AC3 wants. But there might be multiple arming rules; gating all could be intended.

h) AC2: "removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue)". In reconcileReviewVerdicts, the loser for APPROVE is agent:rework, and removeFromIssue only checks issueHasRework for agent:rework loser; for pr_approved loser, removeFromIssue is always false — fine since pr_approved never lives on the issue.

i) One issue: `reconcileDecision` — when the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES and labels are consistent (pr_approved present, agent:rework absent), decision returns null → converged. Good.

j) Potential bug in `latestVerdictForHead` prefix matching: `(head.length >= 7 && records[i].head.indexOf(head) === 0)` — if head is a SHORT sha (7-39 chars) and record head is the full sha, records[i].head starts with head → match. And `(records[i].head.length >= 7 && head.indexOf(records[i].head) === 0)` — record head short (e.g., 7 chars) and probe head full → match. BUT there's a subtle bug: a record with a 7-char head 'aaaa' would also prefix-match a DIFFERENT head that happens to start with those 7 chars — that's fine, 7 hex chars is the standard short-sha ambiguity threshold. But what about a record head of 'h' (test marker with head 'h1'/'h')? For head 'h1' (length 2 < 7), no prefix match — exact only. OK.

However there's an asymmetry issue: records with heads shorter than 7 chars can never prefix-match; only exact. Fine.

Real potential bug: two DIFFERENT heads where one is a prefix of the other (collision of short form is handled, but what about a record head of exactly 40 chars vs probe of 40 chars — exact). Fine.

k) `parseVerdictRecords` sort: records without timestamps get time -1, sinking to front (oldest). Comment says "Unparseable/absent timestamps sink to payload order". OK. But a subtle issue: records with parseable timestamps compare among themselves; a missing timestamp treated as -1 (oldest). That means a malformed record with no `at` loses to any timestamped one — reasonable.

l) The `buildVerdictComment` — `Number(record.blocking || 0) || 0` — for blocking=0 → 0. For "3" → 3. Fine. NaN → 0. OK.

In sm_github.json, the rule has no `skipIfLabel`/`addLabel` — AGENTS.md says "When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label." But this is a localAction with convergent behavior (no dispatch, idempotent by design); skipIfLabel not needed. The hygiene test asserts limit >= 5. Not a violation per se since localActions don't dispatch. Actually the AGENTS.md rule is about preventing re-processing tickets — for localActions like arm_rework, the notLabels guards serve as idempotency. The reconcile rule is convergent. OK.

If there are three records APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, APPROVE (in time order), newest and prev are RC then A... wait order: [APPROVE(t1), REQUEST_CHANGES(t2), APPROVE(t3)] → newest APPROVE(t3), prev REQUEST_CHANGES(t2) → conflict logged, newest wins APPROVE. Not an issue for correctness of reconciliation since newest-wins is what matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

# gh-807: [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Review verdicts must form one reconciled, authoritative state per (PR, head): contradictory verdicts on the same head must be resolved before any arming/merge decision, and the sticky-approval rule must bind the ARming side, not only the rework side.

## Subject

Review-leg verdict posting + tick's arming queries. Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 05:47:30Z and 05:47:40Z — two review legs posted **APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES verdicts 97 seconds apart on the SAME head**; PR state ended contradictory (`pr_approved` + `agent:rework` both applied). Root causes: (a) verdicts are posted as ISSUE comments, so `headMovedSinceLastReview`-style matching can never associate them; (b) no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side ignores the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

## Capability surface

- Verdict persistence: review leg writes a machine-readable verdict record (head sha + verdict + thread census) — file on `factory-data` or a PR comment with a parseable marker, not a free-form issue comment.
- Reconciliation: tick reads the latest verdict per head; if two verdicts exist for one head, newest wins and a WARN is logged; REQUEST_CHANGES from the newest leg blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review.
- Arming-side sticky approval: `agent:rework` arming requires the effective verdict != APPROVE (or unresolved BLOCKING threads), same rule the rework-side uses.
- Clean rollback: reconciliation must not fight the human review state (ruleset approvals untouched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: two verdicts on one head ⇒ tick logs `⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins` and uses the newest.
2. AC2: after reconciliation, `pr_approved` and `agent:rework` cannot coexist on one head (tick removes the loser label with a comment citing both verdict sources).
3. AC3: arming-side check: APPROVE verdict ⇒ no rework arm even when non-blocking threads exist (suggestions do NOT trigger rework).
4. AC4: verdict record is machine-parseable (structured marker), so no head-matching by comment text.
5. AC5: unit tests for the reconciliation; live verification on the next fa GOAL PR with a genuine CHANGES_REQUESTED.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (newest-wins, label reconciliation, APPROVE-blocks-rework-arm).
- L2: replay the #1428 97s-pair against the reconciler.
- L3 (live): one review cycle with contradictory injected verdicts in a scratch PR.

## Non-goals

- Changing what reviewers write in human-readable comments.
- Blocking merges on suggestion-tier threads (only BLOCKING gates).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428, verdicts 05:47:30Z/05:47:40Z 2026-10-09, `pr_approved`+`agent:rework` coexistence.
- Related: #806 (arming latch).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

Potential issues to investigate:

a) In `postPRReviewComments.js`, `postVerdictRecord` uses the global `github_get_pr` directly rather than the scm abstraction. The repo says "SCM abstraction: use js/common/scm.js (via configLoader.createScm(config)) instead of calling github_* or ado_* globals directly." b) In smProvider.verdictRecords — ioCacheGet with kind 'prVerdicts'. Need to check ioCacheGet signature: ioCacheGet(owner, repo, kind, key)? And whether other provider methods use the same pattern. Also, "if (memo) return memo;" — an empty array is truthy? `[]` is truthy in JS, so that's fine. But `null`/`undefined` from a failed... actually ioCachePut always called, so fine.

c) The `latestVerdictRecord(prNumber, headSha)` in smProvider calls `this.verdictRecords(prNumber)` — relies on `this` binding. But one concern: `latestVerdict` guard semantics — `if (q.latestVerdict && (!lvVerdict || q.latestVerdict.indexOf(lvVerdict) === -1)) return false;` — right.

e) The reconcile rule in sm_github.json queries `labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` — OR semantics? Need to verify github source labels query is OR. The test asserts OR semantics ("either contradictory carrier matches (OR semantics — the action decides)"). Let me check githubSource to see how labels filter works. If labels are AND, the rule would match nothing. The test in test_smGithubSource 'latestVerdict: the reconcile rule matches exactly...' uses labels: ['pr_approved', 'agent:rework'] with prs labeled 'pr_approved' and it matched (items pr-81, pr-82). So OR semantics confirmed by test. Good.

f) The arm gate: `reworkArmGate` is computed before `github_add_labels` in arm_rework. But wait — where is `armGate` computed relative to `DRY` check? From diff: DRY check, then armGate, then labels. Good.

g) The arm gate is added to the `arm_rework` localAction in smAgent.js — this gates ALL rules with localAction arm_rework, which is what AC3 wants. But there might be multiple arming rules; gating all could be intended.

h) AC2: "removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue)". In reconcileReviewVerdicts, the loser for APPROVE is agent:rework, and removeFromIssue only checks issueHasRework for agent:rework loser; for pr_approved loser, removeFromIssue is always false — fine since pr_approved never lives on the issue.

i) One issue: `reconcileDecision` — when the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES and labels are consistent (pr_approved present, agent:rework absent), decision returns null → converged. Good.

j) Potential bug in `latestVerdictForHead` prefix matching: `(head.length >= 7 && records[i].head.indexOf(head) === 0)` — if head is a SHORT sha (7-39 chars) and record head is the full sha, records[i].head starts with head → match. And `(records[i].head.length >= 7 && head.indexOf(records[i].head) === 0)` — record head short (e.g., 7 chars) and probe head full → match. BUT there's a subtle bug: a record with a 7-char head 'aaaa' would also prefix-match a DIFFERENT head that happens to start with those 7 chars — that's fine, 7 hex chars is the standard short-sha ambiguity threshold. But what about a record head of 'h' (test marker with head 'h1'/'h')? For head 'h1' (length 2 < 7), no prefix match — exact only. OK.

However there's an asymmetry issue: records with heads shorter than 7 chars can never prefix-match; only exact. Fine.

Real potential bug: two DIFFERENT heads where one is a prefix of the other (collision of short form is handled, but what about a record head of exactly 40 chars vs probe of 40 chars — exact). Fine.

k) `parseVerdictRecords` sort: records without timestamps get time -1, sinking to front (oldest). Comment says "Unparseable/absent timestamps sink to payload order". OK. But a subtle issue: records with parseable timestamps compare among themselves; a missing timestamp treated as -1 (oldest). That means a malformed record with no `at` loses to any timestamped one — reasonable.

l) The `buildVerdictComment` — `Number(record.blocking || 0) || 0` — for blocking=0 → 0. For "3" → 3. Fine. NaN → 0. OK.

m) In postPRReviewComments.postVerdictRecord: uses `issueCounts.blocking` etc. Need to check that issueCounts is in scope at the call site in action() and has those properties. Let me read the surrounding code of action() in postPRReviewComments.js.

In sm_github.json, the rule has no `skipIfLabel`/`addLabel` — AGENTS.md says "When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label." But this is a localAction with convergent behavior (no dispatch, idempotent by design); skipIfLabel not needed. The hygiene test asserts limit >= 5. Not a violation per se since localActions don't dispatch. Actually the AGENTS.md rule is about preventing re-processing tickets — for localActions like arm_rework, the notLabels guards serve as idempotency. The reconcile rule is convergent. OK.

q) Potential issue: the reconcile rule query has `labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` and `latestVerdict: [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]`. The latestVerdict guard requires the newest record for the CURRENT head to exist. For PRs where the reconciliation matters (contradictory), fine. Slight inefficiency: every tick, for up to 10 PRs, fetch PR + comments. With limit 10. OK.

r) AC1 WARN: `latestVerdictForHead` only compares the two NEWEST records for the head. If there are three records APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, APPROVE (in time order), newest and prev are RC then A... wait order: [APPROVE(t1), REQUEST_CHANGES(t2), APPROVE(t3)] → newest APPROVE(t3), prev REQUEST_CHANGES(t2) → conflict logged, newest wins APPROVE. But `latestVerdictForHead` conflict detection compares only the newest TWO records for the head. What about non-adjacent conflicts? Not an issue for correctness of reconciliation since newest-wins is what matters.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

# gh-807: [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Review verdicts must form one reconciled, authoritative state per (PR, head): contradictory verdicts on the same head must be resolved before any arming/merge decision, and the sticky-approval rule must bind the ARming side, not only the rework side.

## Subject

Review-leg verdict posting + tick's arming queries. Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 05:47:30Z and 05:47:40Z — two review legs posted **APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES verdicts 97 seconds apart on the SAME head**; PR state ended contradictory (`pr_approved` + `agent:rework` both applied). Root causes: (a) verdicts are posted as ISSUE comments, so `headMovedSinceLastReview`-style matching can never associate them; (b) no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side ignores the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

## Capability surface

- Verdict persistence: review leg writes a machine-readable verdict record (head sha + verdict + thread census) — file on `factory-data` or a PR comment with a parseable marker, not a free-form issue comment.
- Reconciliation: tick reads the latest verdict per head; if two verdicts exist for one head, newest wins and a WARN is logged; REQUEST_CHANGES from the newest leg blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review.
- Arming-side sticky approval: `agent:rework` arming requires the effective verdict != APPROVE (or unresolved BLOCKING threads), same rule the rework-side uses.
- Clean rollback: reconciliation must not fight the human review state (ruleset approvals untouched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: two verdicts on one head ⇒ tick logs `⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins` and uses the newest.
2. AC2: after reconciliation, `pr_approved` and `agent:rework` cannot coexist on one head (tick removes the loser label with a comment citing both verdict sources).
3. AC3: arming-side check: APPROVE verdict ⇒ no rework arm even when non-blocking threads exist (suggestions do NOT trigger rework).
4. AC4: verdict record is machine-parseable (structured marker), so no head-matching by comment text.
5. AC5: unit tests for the reconciliation; live verification on the next fa GOAL PR with a genuine CHANGES_REQUESTED.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (newest-wins, label reconciliation, APPROVE-blocks-rework-arm).
- L2: replay the #1428 97s-pair against the reconciler.
- L3 (live): one review cycle with contradictory injected verdicts in a scratch PR.

## Non-goals

- Changing what reviewers write in human-readable comments.
- Blocking merges on suggestion-tier threads (only BLOCKING gates).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428, verdicts 05:47:30Z/05:47:40Z 2026-10-09, `pr_approved`+`agent:rework` coexistence.
- Related: #806 (arming latch).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

blocks.text:
Now let me read the full source files for the changed files to get complete context. Key things to check:

1. `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` — full file (I've seen it all in the diff since it's new).
2. `js/common/smProvider.js` — check ioCacheGet/ioCachePut usage and how ioCache interacts; check that `verdictRecords` handles cache correctly.
3. `js/postPRReviewComments.js` — check where postVerdictRecord is called and where issueCounts comes from; verify repoInfo shape; check that `github_get_pr` is a bridge global there; check `scm.addComment` signature.
4. `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` — check the guard ordering and needsStatus logic.
5. `js/smAgent.js` — check reconcile_verdicts & arm_rework placement in processRule; check `ticket.issueNumber` availability; check github_remove_label global; check that arm_rework's reworkArmGate is only invoked in the right place.

Potential issues to investigate:

a) In `postPRReviewComments.js`, `postVerdictRecord` uses the global `github_get_pr` directly rather than the scm abstraction. The repo says "SCM abstraction: use js/common/scm.js (via configLoader.createScm(config)) instead of calling github_* or ado_* globals directly." But postPRReviewComments.js is GitHub-specific (posting to GitHub PR), and it already uses `gh` helpers. Let me check if postPRReviewComments.js already uses github_* globals elsewhere. Let me grep.

b) In smProvider.verdictRecords — ioCacheGet with kind 'prVerdicts'. Need to check ioCacheGet signature: ioCacheGet(owner, repo, kind, key)? And whether other provider methods use the same pattern. Also, "if (memo) return memo;" — an empty array is truthy? `[]` is truthy in JS, so that's fine. But `null`/`undefined` from a failed... actually ioCachePut always called, so fine.

c) The `latestVerdictRecord(prNumber, headSha)` in smProvider calls `this.verdictRecords(prNumber)` — relies on `this` binding. In githubSource.js: `provider.latestVerdictRecord(item.prNumber, item.pr && item.pr.headSha)` — called as method, so `this` is provider. OK. But if destructured elsewhere it would break. Let me check for other call sites.

d) In githubSource.js matchesGuards — where is the guard placed relative to other guards? It's placed after the staleVerdict guard and before threadsResolved. Fine. But one concern: `latestVerdict` guard semantics — `if (q.latestVerdict && (!lvVerdict || q.latestVerdict.indexOf(lvVerdict) === -1)) return false;` — right.

e) The reconcile rule in sm_github.json queries `labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` — OR semantics? Need to verify github source labels query is OR. The test asserts OR semantics ("either contradictory carrier matches (OR semantics — the action decides)"). Let me check githubSource to see how labels filter works. If labels are AND, the rule would match nothing. The test in test_smGithubSource 'latestVerdict: the reconcile rule matches exactly...' uses labels: ['pr_approved', 'agent:rework'] with prs labeled 'pr_approved' and it matched (items pr-81, pr-82). So OR semantics confirmed by test. Good.

f) The arm gate: `reworkArmGate` is computed before `github_add_labels` in arm_rework. But wait — where is `armGate` computed relative to `DRY` check? From diff: DRY check, then armGate, then labels. Good.

g) The arm gate is added to the `arm_rework` localAction in smAgent.js — this gates ALL rules with localAction arm_rework, which is what AC3 wants. But there might be multiple arming rules; gating all could be intended.

h) AC2: "removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue)". In reconcileReviewVerdicts, the loser for APPROVE is agent:rework, and removeFromIssue only checks issueHasRework for agent:rework loser; for pr_approved loser, removeFromIssue is always false — fine since pr_approved never lives on the issue.

i) One issue: `reconcileDecision` — when the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES and labels are consistent (pr_approved present, agent:rework absent), decision returns null → converged. Good.

j) Potential bug in `latestVerdictForHead` prefix matching: `(head.length >= 7 && records[i].head.indexOf(head) === 0)` — if head is a SHORT sha (7-39 chars) and record head is the full sha, records[i].head starts with head → match. And `(records[i].head.length >= 7 && head.indexOf(records[i].head) === 0)` — record head short (e.g., 7 chars) and probe head full → match. BUT there's a subtle bug: a record with a 7-char head 'aaaa' would also prefix-match a DIFFERENT head that happens to start with those 7 chars — that's fine, 7 hex chars is the standard short-sha ambiguity threshold. But what about a record head of 'h' (test marker with head 'h1'/'h')? For head 'h1' (length 2 < 7), no prefix match — exact only. OK.

However there's an asymmetry issue: records with heads shorter than 7 chars can never prefix-match; only exact. Fine.

Real potential bug: two DIFFERENT heads where one is a prefix of the other (collision of short form is handled, but what about a record head of exactly 40 chars vs probe of 40 chars — exact). Fine.

k) `parseVerdictRecords` sort: records without timestamps get time -1, sinking to front (oldest). Comment says "Unparseable/absent timestamps sink to payload order". OK. But a subtle issue: records with parseable timestamps compare among themselves; a missing timestamp treated as -1 (oldest). That means a malformed record with no `at` loses to any timestamped one — reasonable.

l) The `buildVerdictComment` — `Number(record.blocking || 0) || 0` — for blocking=0 → 0. For "3" → 3. Fine. NaN → 0. OK.

m) In postPRReviewComments.postVerdictRecord: uses `issueCounts.blocking` etc. Need to check that issueCounts is in scope at the call site in action() and has those properties. Let me read the surrounding code of action() in postPRReviewComments.js.

n) In postVerdictRecord, the call `scm.addComment(prNumber, body)` — check scm.addComment signature used elsewhere in the same file. Let me grep.

o) In smAgent.js reconcile_verdicts: uses `github_remove_label` global — check that this global exists and is used elsewhere in smAgent.js. Also `github_create_comment` with `number` param — check other usages for param name consistency (number vs prNumber/issueNumber).

p) Rule placement: reconcile-review-verdicts placed after rerun twins. In sm_github.json, the rule has no `skipIfLabel`/`addLabel` — AGENTS.md says "When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label." But this is a localAction with convergent behavior (no dispatch, idempotent by design); skipIfLabel not needed. The hygiene test asserts limit >= 5. Not a violation per se since localActions don't dispatch. Actually the AGENTS.md rule is about preventing re-processing tickets — for localActions like arm_rework, the notLabels guards serve as idempotency. The reconcile rule is convergent. OK.

q) Potential issue: the reconcile rule query has `labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` and `latestVerdict: [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]`. The latestVerdict guard requires the newest record for the CURRENT head to exist. For PRs where the reconciliation matters (contradictory), fine. But consider: PR with pr_approved and a single newest APPROVE record → reconcileDecision returns null (nothing to remove) → "already agree". Converges each tick, no harm. Slight inefficiency: every tick, for up to 10 PRs, fetch PR + comments. With limit 10. OK.

r) AC1 WARN: `latestVerdictForHead` only compares the two NEWEST records for the head. If there are three records APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, APPROVE (in time order), newest and prev are RC then A... wait order: [APPROVE(t1), REQUEST_CHANGES(t2), APPROVE(t3)] → newest APPROVE(t3), prev REQUEST_CHANGES(t2) → conflict logged, newest wins APPROVE. Fine.

s) Now a REAL potential correctness issue: the reconcile rule removes `pr_approved` when newest is REQUEST_CHANGES — good. But `latestVerdictForHead` conflict detection compares only the newest TWO records for the head. What about non-adjacent conflicts? Not an issue for correctness of reconciliation since newest-wins is what matters.

t) Another potential issue: `verdictRecords` in smProvider uses `ioCacheGet(owner, repo, 'prVerdicts', prNumber)` and `ioCachePut`. Need to check …

- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -12
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

# gh-807: [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)

## Description

## Goal

Review verdicts must form one reconciled, authoritative state per (PR, head): contradictory verdicts on the same head must be resolved before any arming/merge decision, and the sticky-approval rule must bind the ARming side, not only the rework side.

## Subject

Review-leg verdict posting + tick's arming queries. Evidence: fa PR #1428, 2026-10-09 05:47:30Z and 05:47:40Z — two review legs posted **APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES verdicts 97 seconds apart on the SAME head**; PR state ended contradictory (`pr_approved` + `agent:rework` both applied). Root causes: (a) verdicts are posted as ISSUE comments, so `headMovedSinceLastReview`-style matching can never associate them; (b) no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side ignores the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

## Capability surface

- Verdict persistence: review leg writes a machine-readable verdict record (head sha + verdict + thread census) — file on `factory-data` or a PR comment with a parseable marker, not a free-form issue comment.
- Reconciliation: tick reads the latest verdict per head; if two verdicts exist for one head, newest wins and a WARN is logged; REQUEST_CHANGES from the newest leg blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review.
- Arming-side sticky approval: `agent:rework` arming requires the effective verdict != APPROVE (or unresolved BLOCKING threads), same rule the rework-side uses.
- Clean rollback: reconciliation must not fight the human review state (ruleset approvals untouched).

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: two verdicts on one head ⇒ tick logs `⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins` and uses the newest.
2. AC2: after reconciliation, `pr_approved` and `agent:rework` cannot coexist on one head (tick removes the loser label with a comment citing both verdict sources).
3. AC3: arming-side check: APPROVE verdict ⇒ no rework arm even when non-blocking threads exist (suggestions do NOT trigger rework).
4. AC4: verdict record is machine-parseable (structured marker), so no head-matching by comment text.
5. AC5: unit tests for the reconciliation; live verification on the next fa GOAL PR with a genuine CHANGES_REQUESTED.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (newest-wins, label reconciliation, APPROVE-blocks-rework-arm).
- L2: replay the #1428 97s-pair against the reconciler.
- L3 (live): one review cycle with contradictory injected verdicts in a scratch PR.

## Non-goals

- Changing what reviewers write in human-readable comments.
- Blocking merges on suggestion-tier threads (only BLOCKING gates).

## References

- Forensics: fa PR #1428, verdicts 05:47:30Z/05:47:40Z 2026-10-09, `pr_approved`+`agent:rework` coexistence.
- Related: #806 (arming latch).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
