{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. **Red-CI rework flow (the STANDARD sticky-approval flow!):**
- head H: pr_approved + APPROVE record (blocking 0). Validation red. fail-validation requeues agent:rework on issue.
- Next tick: reconcile (rule 3) strips agent:rework from the issue + posts ⚖️ comment. rework-on-red-ci (rule ~31) then queries issue items with agent:rework → **nothing** → no dispatch this tick.
- If the leg was already dispatched in the previous tick (same tick as fail-validation, because ordering: reconcile 3 < fail-validation 12 < rework-on-red-ci 31 — so requeue+dispatch happen same tick T1, and reconcile first acts at T2 when the label is already sticky) — leg in flight, pushes → head moves → recovery: reconcile stops matching (head H record no longer matches head H2), labels stop being stripped.
- **BUT if the dispatched leg dies without pushing** (the dead-letter case the sticky issue label exists for): tick T3+ — reconcile strips the label at rule 3 BEFORE rework-on-red-ci queries → no re-fire; fail-validation can't re-fire (no ai_validating arm on the PR anymore — it was unarmed in T1; the head is still red; nothing re-arms validation: validate-armed needs ai_validating... validate-fresh needs checks none/pending — head is red → no). **The PR strands: red head + pr_approved + no rework arm + no validation arm.** Actually wait — validate-fresh-masked-green requires green. revalidate rules need ai_validating. Both are core designed flows on sticky-approved PRs. The reconcile rule treats the coexistence as the #1428 pathology — but #1428 was REVIEW-driven contradiction, not CI-driven rework. This is a genuine correctness bug: the reconciliation's loser-label resolution ignores the arm's source. An APPROVE verdict does not invalidate a red-CI rework arm.

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

**Suggested fix** (small): in `reconcileReviewVerdicts`, skip stripping `agent:rework` when the head has a real CI failure — the existing `headHasRealFailure(repoInfo, headSha)` probe — or pass an `armIsCiDriven`/`checksRed` fact into `reconcileDecision`'s state. Then add a unit replay: APPROVE record + red checks + issue armed by fail-validation ⇒ arm survives, no comment.

- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

**Suggested fix** (small): in `reconcileReviewVerdicts`, skip stripping `agent:rework` when the head has a real CI failure — the existing `headHasRealFailure(repoInfo, headSha)` probe — or pass an `armIsCiDriven`/`checksRed` fact into `reconcileDecision`'s state. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

**Suggested fix** (small): in `reconcileReviewVerdicts`, skip stripping `agent:rework` when the head has a real CI failure — the existing `headHasRealFailure(repoInfo, headSha)` probe — or pass an `armIsCiDriven`/`checksRed` fact into `reconcileDecision`'s state. Then add a unit replay: APPROVE record + red checks + issue armed by fail-validation ⇒ arm survives, no comment.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the rule matches every approved PR forever, every tick**

`labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` + `latestVerdict: [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` matches **any** PR that carries `pr_approved` (sticky until merge) with a verdict record on its head — i.e. essentially every approved PR from the first review onward, converged or not. Consider splitting into the two conflict-shaped queries so the standing match set shrinks to ~zero:

- `labels: [agent:rework]` + `latestVerdict: [APPROVE]` (rework arm next to an approval — the #1428 shape)
- `labels: [pr_approved]` + `latestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` (stale approval next to a changes-requested verdict)

Both localActions can stay as-is; only the queries change.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC1 conflict WARN re-logs on every guard evaluation for the head's lifetime**

`latestVerdictForHead` WARNs on **every call** when the two newest records for a head differ — and records never expire, so after reconciliation (or on any head that ever saw two different verdicts) every subsequent tick logs the identical line once per guard evaluation: the reconcile rule, `notLatestVerdict` on merge-validated/validate-armed/revalidate-armed/revalidate-armed-green, and the arm gate — 5-6 identical WARNs per tick per PR until the head moves or merges. I see the rule ordering. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is at index ~62 (3rd rule), and rules like `rework-on-red-ci` (dispatch leg on issue agent:rework) and `rework-on-label` (PR-anchored) are later. Key part of the rework-on-red-ci description:

"agent:rework can sit on BOTH carriers at once — the issue (this rule) AND the PR (armed by rework-unresolved-threads...)... notPrLabels agent:rework makes this rule defer to the PR-carrier rule whenever the PR is armed: rework-on-label is PR-anchored (the #544-safe anchor), consumes its label on dispatch... No consumeLabels here by design: the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on); the issue-anchored leg itself clears the label via pr_rework removeLabels."

So the ISSUE-carrier agent:rework label is deliberately sticky — it survives dispatch as dead-letter recovery ("the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired"). 

**Now the AC2/AC3 conflict materializes clearly:**

Scenario A (legitimate blocking-threads rework destroyed by reconciliation):
1. Review leg stamps APPROVE with blocking=2 on head H (allowApproveWithSuggestions=true or the census is just what the reviewer recorded), leaves unresolved BLOCKING threads.
2. rework-unresolved-threads arms agent:rework on the PR (blocking-threads exception — the arm is CORRECT per AC3).
3. Same tick, later: rework-on-label dispatches and consumes the PR label. Issue label? Not involved here. OK — the PR carrier is consumed on dispatch.

Scenario B (dead-letter recovery destroyed): the rework leg is armed on the ISSUE (by conflict-rework or fail-validation's requeue or review RC re-arm). Suppose the rework leg fails to start (dead letter). The issue keeps agent:rework so the leg re-fires. Now someone/something gets an APPROVE record on the current head... e.g., a stale head? No — records match per head. If the current head has an APPROVE record while the issue is armed for rework: reconcile strips the issue's agent:rework → dead-letter recovery destroyed. When would a head have an APPROVE record AND the issue be armed for rework? 
- conflict-rework arms the issue (DIRTY head) — head has an older APPROVE record from when the head was clean? The record was stamped on the same head sha (records ride heads, not states). A head that was APPROVE-stamped then went DIRTY after main moved... the record is still on that sha. conflict-rework arms the issue → reconcile (rule 3, BEFORE conflict-rework at ~358) next tick: current head H still carries APPROVE record → loser agent:rework → strips from issue → conflict-rework RE-ARMS (later rule same tick) → marker? This is a strip/re-arm yo-yo WITH a reconciliation comment posted EVERY tick (reconcile posts a comment each time it removes something!). Comment spam + label churn every tick, plus the reconciliation actively fights conflict-rework's arm. Hmm wait — order: reconcile (rule 3) strips; conflict-rework (rule ~30) re-arms. Next tick: reconcile strips again (record still APPROVE on head H, issue has agent:rework again) → posts ANOTHER comment → conflict-rework re-arms... infinite yo-yo with one comment per tick per PR. Until the head moves (rework fixes conflicts and pushes) or the verdict changes. The rework DOES eventually fire (dispatch isn't blocked by reconcile), the rework leg pushes → new head → records fail-open → arm survives. {"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

**Suggested fix** (small): in `reconcileReviewVerdicts`, skip stripping `agent:rework` when the head has a real CI failure — the existing `headHasRealFailure(repoInfo, headSha)` probe — or pass an `armIsCiDriven`/`checksRed` fact into `reconcileDecision`'s state. Then add a unit replay: APPROVE record + red checks + issue armed by fail-validation ⇒ arm survives, no comment.

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The verdict-record protocol, per-head newest-wins resolution, arming-side sticky-approval gate and fail-open wiring are solid and well-tested (full suite locally green: 2042 passed, 0 failed). One blocking correctness gap: `reconcileDecision` treats *every* `agent:rework` label as a review-driven arm, so an APPROVE verdict record on the head makes the tick strip the red-CI rework arms that `fail-validation`/`conflict-rework` legitimately place next to a sticky approval — killing the dead-letter re-fire path and re-introducing the exact PR-strand deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed, plus a ⚖️ comment per tick while the arm yo-yos.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING (1): APPROVE-winner reconciliation strips CI-driven (and manual human) `agent:rework` arms; the rule runs before the rework dispatch rules, so a dead rework leg is never re-fired on a red approved head (js/common/reviewVerdicts.js `resolveLoserLabel`/`reconcileDecision` + sm_github.json rule order).
- 💡 SUGGESTION (2): reconcile rule matches every sticky-approved PR every tick (constant per-tick API cost); conflict WARN re-logs per guard evaluation for the head's lifetime.

1. Exempt heads with a real CI failure from the APPROVE-winner `agent:rework` strip (reuse `headHasRealFailure`), or restrict the strip to review-driven/both-carrier shapes; add the red-CI replay test.

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). The PR strands red + approved with no leg: the exact deadlock class gh-683/gh-710 fixed.
3. **`conflict-rework` arms** (DIRTY head) are re-added every tick and stripped again by rule #3 → a strip/re-add yo-yo with one ⚖️ comment per tick (the same yo-yo class gh-751 eliminated).
4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.

**Suggested fix** (small): in `reconcileReviewVerdicts`, skip stripping `agent:rework` when the head has a real CI failure — the existing `headHasRealFailure(repoInfo, headSha)` probe — or pass an `armIsCiDriven`/`checksRed` fact into `reconcileDecision`'s state. Then add a unit replay: APPROVE record + red checks + issue armed by fail-validation ⇒ arm survives, no comment.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the rule matches every approved PR forever, every tick**

`labels: [pr_approved, agent:rework]` + `latestVerdict: [APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` matches **any** PR that carries `pr_approved` (sticky until merge) with a verdict record on its head — i.e. essentially every approved PR from the first review onward, converged or not. Each tick that is `github_get_pr` + `github_get_pr_comments` + `github_get_issue` per matched PR (limit 10) just to log "already agree".

Consider splitting into the two conflict-shaped queries so the standing match set shrinks to ~zero:

- `labels: [agent:rework]` + `latestVerdict: [APPROVE]` (rework arm next to an approval — the #1428 shape)
- `labels: [pr_approved]` + `latestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` (stale approval next to a changes-requested verdict)

Both localActions can stay as-is; only the queries change.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC1 conflict WARN re-logs on every guard evaluation for the head's lifetime**

`latestVerdictForHead` WARNs on **every call** when the two newest records for a head differ — and records never expire, so after reconciliation (or on any head that ever saw two different verdicts) every subsequent tick logs the identical line once per guard evaluation: the reconcile rule, `notLatestVerdict` on merge-validated/validate-armed/revalidate-armed/revalidate-armed-green, and the arm gate — 5-6 identical WARNs per tick per PR until the head moves or merges. The module doc acknowledges "logged once per call", but the callers are per-rule-per-tick.

Consider de-duplicating (e.g. a module-level `warnedHeads` set keyed by head+verdict-pair) or moving the WARN to the reconcile path only, keeping the guard-layer calls silent consumers of `effective.conflict`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 810
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/810
- **Title**: gh-807 [BUG] Contradictory review verdicts on one head are never reconciled — APPROVE + REQUEST_CHANGES 97s apart left pr_approved and agent:rework coexisting (fa PR #1428)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-807` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1968
- **Deletions**: -294
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T07:12:05Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T08:04:12Z

## PR Description

Closes #807
### Root Cause

Two review legs concluded on the same PR head 97s apart with contradictory verdicts (fa PR #1428: APPROVE at 05:47:30Z, REQUEST_CHANGES at 05:47:40Z) and both side effects stuck — `pr_approved` + `agent:rework` coexisting. Three composing defects: (a) verdicts were free-form comments with no head association, so head-matching probes can never tie a verdict to a head; (b) the SM tick had no verdict-reconciliation step; (c) the arming side (`arm_rework`) ignored the sticky-approval rule the rework side enforces.

### Fix

- `js/common/reviewVerdicts.js` (new): the verdict-record protocol — structured marker `<!-- dmtools:review-verdict {head, verdict, blocking, important, suggestions, at, source} -->`; newest-wins per head with the AC1 conflict WARN (`⚠️ verdict conflict on <head>: APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES — newest wins`); loser-label resolution; reconciliation comment citing both verdict sources; the arming gate. Pure module, fully unit-tested.
- `js/postPRReviewComments.js`: the review leg stamps the machine-parseable record on the PR (head sha required — no head-less verdicts; records what the leg actually did after approve-with-suggestions overrides). Non-fatal, both anchored and PR-anchored paths.
- `js/smAgent.js`: new `reconcile_verdicts` localAction — removes the loser label from BOTH carriers (PR + linked issue) with one comment citing both verdict sources (AC2); `arm_rework` now withholds the arm when the effective verdict is APPROVE with zero BLOCKING findings — suggestions never trigger rework (AC3). Both fail open for pre-gh-807 PRs without records.
- `js/sm/sources/githubSource.js` + `js/common/smProvider.js`: `latestVerdict` / `notLatestVerdict` query guards over the newest record for the current head (ioCache-memoized, fail-open); verdict-guard rules now fetch prStatus (the guards need the head sha).
- `sm_github.json`: new `reconcile-review-verdicts` rule (localAction `reconcile_verdicts`) placed after the rerun twins and before the merge window (#682/#637 invariants untouched); `notLatestVerdict: [REQUEST_CHANGES, BLOCK]` on merge-validated, validate-armed, revalidate-armed, revalidate-armed-green — a newest REQUEST_CHANGES blocks `pr_approved`-gated paths until re-review. Human review state / ruleset approvals untouched.

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewVerdicts.js` (new, 20 tests): marker protocol (AC4 — free-form verdict text is invisible), #1428 replay with the exact AC1 WARN, AC2 reconciliation both directions, AC3 arm gate incl. the blocking-thread exception and fail-opens.
- `test_smAgent.js` (+17): #1428 reconciliation replay, both-carriers removal, converged/no-record/text-only no-ops, arm gate (withheld / blocking-exception / changes-requested / legacy), rule hygiene (placement + `notLatestVerdict` lanes).
- `test_smGithubSource.js` (+5), `test_smProvider.js` (+5), `test_postPRReviewComments.js` (+5): guard semantics + needsStatus wiring, provider memoization/fail-open, record posting.
- RED verified: with pre-fix code the #1428 replay and the arming-gate tests fail (arm still fires, no reconciliation); GREEN: full suite `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — 2019 passed, 0 failed (baseline 1974).

### Notes

- Fail-open everywhere: PRs without verdict records (pre-gh-807) reconcile nothing and arm as before — no behavior change for legacy PRs.
- Only machine-owned labels reconcile; ruleset approvals and human review comments are never touched (clean rollback).
- GitLab gets the guards as inert (no MR-note reader in the tool catalog yet) — documented gap in `smProvider.js`; reconciliation is GitHub-machine-loop behavior for now.
- Live L3 (one review cycle with injected contradictory verdicts on a scratch PR) is pending — needs the next fa tick run against a real deployment.

But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

{"content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: Reconciliation strips CI-driven `agent:rework` arms and breaks red-CI dead-letter recovery**

`resolveLoserLabel('APPROVE')` unconditionally makes `agent:rework` the loser, and `reconcileDecision` strips it from **both** carriers whenever it is present. But an APPROVE verdict record does **not** invalidate every rework arm — `agent:rework` has non-review sources that legitimately coexist with an APPROVE record on the same head:

1. **Red-CI rework on a sticky-approved PR (the standard flow).** `fail_validation` (smAgent.js ~2845) re-arms `agent:rework` on the linked issue when validation goes red — documented as "pr_approved is STICKY … Validation red post-approval re-arms rework only". That head carries the APPROVE record the review leg just stamped. `reconcile-review-verdicts` is rule #3 — it runs **before** `fail-validation` and before the `rework-on-red-ci` dispatch — so on the very next tick it strips the issue's `agent:rework` and posts a ⚖️ comment saying "suggestions do not justify a rework arm" (factually wrong: it was a red-CI arm).
2. **Dead-letter recovery destroyed.** The issue carrier is sticky *by design*: "the issue arm must survive dispatch so a failed/never-started leg is re-fired (the dead-letter recovery the machine loop is built on)" (rework-on-red-ci description). Once reconcile strips the label ahead of the dispatch rule's query, a dead/never-started rework leg is never re-fired — and `fail-validation` cannot re-arm either (`ai_validating` is already consumed and nothing re-arms validation on a red head). 4. **Manual human `agent:rework` labels** (rework-on-label honors them for ANY author) are silently stripped the same way — despite the stated "only machine-owned labels reconcile" guarantee.

The hygiene test asserts `fail-validation` stays `notLatestVerdict`-neutral ("red CI arms rework regardless of which review verdict is newest") — but the reconcile **action** is not verdict-neutral on the arm side, so the invariant only holds at the query layer.
